description: Experience the soulful warmth of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas. This comforting and healthy soup is a staple in Middle Eastern homes, cherished for its rich flavor, vibrant color, and nourishing ingredients. Made with simple pantry items, it offers a taste of authentic Lebanese hospitality in every spoonful, perfect for a cozy meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and dice the carrot and potato into small, uniform pieces. This ensures even cooking and a smooth texture.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saute for 5-7 minutes, until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Vegetables and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the diced carrot and potato, cooking for 3-4 minutes. Add the rinsed red lentils, ground cumin, and turmeric powder (if using). Stir everything together for about 1 minute, allowing the spices to toast slightly.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Blend to Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Carefully remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches your desired consistency. For a smoother soup, blend completely; for a chunkier soup, blend only half. Alternatively, transfer portions to a regular blender (be careful with hot liquids).

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Return the pot to low heat. Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. The lemon is crucial for balancing the flavors. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water.

instructions.title: Prepare Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: For an authentic touch, in a small pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil and lightly toast the dried mint for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of fresh cilantro or parsley and the toasted dried mint. Serve immediately with a side of pita bread or a fresh salad.

tips: Always rinse your lentils thoroughly before cooking to remove any dust or debris and to ensure a clearer soup broth.
For the best flavor, do not skip the fresh lemon juice at the end; it brightens the soup significantly and is a hallmark of authentic Adas.
Store leftover soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as "Adas" in Arabic, is more than just a dish; it's a warm embrace in a bowl. This humble yet incredibly flavorful soup is a cornerstone of Middle Eastern cuisine, cherished for its nourishing qualities, ease of preparation, and comforting aroma. Whether you're seeking a hearty meal on a chilly evening, a light and healthy lunch, or a taste of authentic Lebanese tradition, Adas delivers. Made from simple, wholesome ingredients, this vibrant red lentil soup is naturally vegetarian, often vegan, and packed with plant-based protein and essential nutrients. Dive with us into the world of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup and discover why it’s a beloved staple across the globe.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

At its heart, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a testament to the power of simple ingredients to create profound flavor. "Adas" is the Arabic word for lentils, and in this context, it specifically refers to a soup made predominantly with red lentils. Unlike other lentil soups that might feature a multitude of vegetables or complex spice blends, Adas shines through its elegant simplicity. The core components usually include red lentils, sautéed onions and garlic, often carrots for sweetness and body, and a distinctive bright finish from fresh lemon juice. Cumin is the dominant spice, lending an earthy warmth that perfectly complements the lentils. This soup is a staple in Lebanese households, particularly during the cooler months, as a comforting meal, or during religious fasting periods due to its nourishing and meat-free nature. Its naturally creamy texture, even without dairy, makes it incredibly satisfying.

## Ingredients for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Crafting the perfect Lebanese Red Lentil Soup requires a few key ingredients, each playing a crucial role in its distinct flavor profile:

*   **Red Lentils:** Split red lentils are preferred as they cook quickly and break down easily, contributing to the soup's creamy texture.
*   **Olive Oil:** A good quality extra virgin olive oil is essential for sautéing and for a final drizzle, adding richness and authentic flavor.
*   **Aromatics:** Yellow onion and fresh garlic form the flavorful base. A carrot is often included for natural sweetness and depth.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** Either works, but a good vegetable broth will enhance the overall flavor.
*   **Spices:** Ground cumin is non-negotiable, providing warmth and earthiness. A pinch of turmeric adds a beautiful golden color and subtle flavor. Salt and freshly ground black pepper are also vital for seasoning.
*   **Lemon Juice:** Freshly squeezed lemon juice is perhaps the most critical finishing touch, adding a vibrant tang that brightens the entire soup.
*   **Fresh Herbs (for garnish):** Fresh cilantro or parsley chopped finely, or even fresh mint, adds a burst of freshness and color upon serving.

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup: Step-by-Step

Making Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, even for novice cooks. Follow these steps for a delicious bowl of Adas:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing your red lentils under cold water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and helps prevent a cloudy soup. Drain well.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and chopped carrot, cooking for another 3-5 minutes until slightly tender and fragrant.
3.  **Add Lentils and Spices:** Stir in the rinsed and drained red lentils, ground cumin, turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Sauté for about 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to lightly toast the spices and lentils, which deepens their flavor.
4.  **Simmer:** Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer gently. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface during the initial simmering.
5.  **Achieve Desired Consistency:** For a smoother soup, use an immersion blender directly in the pot, or carefully transfer batches to a standard blender (vent the lid!). Blend until you reach your desired creamy consistency. Many traditional recipes leave it slightly chunky for texture.
6.  **Finish and Season:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice. Taste the Lebanese Red Lentil Soup and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference.

## Tips for the Best Adas Soup

Achieving that perfect, soul-warming bowl of Adas is easy with a few simple tips:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This step is crucial for clarity and removes any starchy residue that can make your soup gummy.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Lemon:** Fresh lemon juice is the defining characteristic of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup. Add it at the very end to preserve its bright, fresh flavor. Taste and add more if you like a tangier soup.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** Use a good quality extra virgin olive oil for both sautéing and a final drizzle before serving. It adds a subtle fruitiness and richness.
*   **Cumin is Key:** Cumin is the star spice here. Ensure it's fresh and fragrant for the best results.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** As with any soup, tasting and adjusting seasoning throughout the cooking process, especially at the end, is vital. Salt, pepper, and lemon can make all the difference.
*   **Watch the Consistency:** If the soup becomes too thick during simmering, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency.

## Serving Suggestions for Red Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is wonderfully versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways. Traditionally, it's served hot, garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro or parsley, and a final drizzle of good olive oil.

*   **With Pita Bread:** Scoop up every delicious bite with warm, soft pita bread, either plain or toasted.
*   **Fresh Vegetables:** A side plate of fresh vegetables like radishes, scallions, or mint leaves provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always offer extra lemon wedges on the side for those who prefer an even brighter, tangier flavor.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For a touch of heat, sprinkle a pinch of Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes on top.
*   **Simple Salad:** Pair it with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil for a complete and light meal.
*   **Pickles:** Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips or cucumbers) offer a delightful sour counterpoint to the soup's richness.

## Variations & Substitutions for Lebanese Lentil Soup

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup recipe is perfect as is, it's also quite adaptable to your preferences or what you have on hand:

*   **Add More Vegetables:** Feel free to bulk up the soup with other finely diced vegetables like celery, zucchini, spinach, or Swiss chard during the last few minutes of cooking. Potatoes or sweet potatoes can add extra heartiness and a touch of sweetness.
*   **Spice It Up:** For a different flavor profile, a pinch of allspice or a very small amount of cinnamon can be added along with the cumin. A little cayenne pepper can introduce a pleasant warmth.
*   **Herbs:** While cilantro and parsley are common, fresh or dried mint can also be a wonderful addition, stirred in at the end.
*   **Broth Choice:** While vegetable broth keeps it vegetarian/vegan, some prefer chicken broth for added depth of flavor.
*   **Texture Play:** If you prefer a heartier, chunkier soup, simply mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot with a spoon instead of blending.
*   **Tomato Paste:** A tablespoon of tomato paste can be added with the aromatics to give the soup a richer color and a subtle umami note.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a testament to the fact that the most satisfying dishes often come from the simplest ingredients. Its comforting warmth, vibrant flavors, and incredible nutritional value make it a beloved dish across the Middle East and beyond. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a kitchen novice, whipping up a batch of Adas is a rewarding experience that promises a bowl full of wholesome deliciousness. Give this classic Middle Eastern soup a try, and discover your new favorite comfort food.
